solution:
Let \(\alpha\) be the common root, so \(a\alpha^2 + b\alpha + c = 0\) and \(p\alpha^2 + q\alpha + r = 0\).
By cross-multiplication, \(\dfrac{\alpha^2}{br - cq} = \dfrac{\alpha}{cp - ar} = \dfrac{1}{aq - bp}\).
So \(\alpha = \dfrac{cp - ar}{aq - bp}\) and \(\alpha^2 = \dfrac{br - cq}{aq - bp}\).
Squaring the first and equating with the second: \(\dfrac{(cp - ar)^2}{(aq - bp)^2} = \dfrac{br - cq}{aq - bp}\), so \((cp - ar)^2 = (br - cq)(aq - bp)\).
Since \((cp - ar)^2 = (ar - cp)^2\), the condition is \((ar - cp)^2 = (br - cq)(aq - bp)\), which is option B.
note: the solution stated the condition as (br - cq)^2 = (ar - cp)(aq - bp), with the squared and product terms swapped, which matches no option and contradicts the key; elimination gives (ar - cp)^2 = (br - cq)(aq - bp), the keyed option B.
